Subject: AcmePay - Post-demo performance SLO recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Lena,

Thanks again for the time today — great to see the AcmePay demo go through your real load patterns. Per our discussion, I captured the performance SLOs and the immediate next steps below so we can align the MAP and the trial configuration.

High-level SLOs (from today's call)
- Latency: p95 target < 200 ms (interactive UI flows)
- Latency: p99 target target discussed as 350-450 ms (Samir asked to confirm)
- Throughput: sustain 500 req/s for 10+ minutes during peak windows
- Concurrency: support 100+ concurrent user sessions with KV cache warmed
- Streaming: yes — token-by-token streaming required for live UI (TTF target < 200 ms for first tokens)
- Cold-starts: warm pool preferred; cold-starts should fall back to lower QoS (we discussed warm pool sizing)

Attachments included: slo-checklist.pdf (detailed checklist), demo-results.csv (sample traces). I've also attached our internal perf matrix for the demo (acmepay-perf-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps / MAP items
1) Confirm decision criteria (latency/throughput/concurrency) — action: Samir
2) Redwood to run a focused perf test against a production-like workload — action: Marissa; target week of Feb 20
3) Provide a short-lived test account and sample payloads + perf test plan link — action: Marissa (see link below)
4) If perf test meets criteria, enable a 2-week dedicated trial (reserved capacity) and draft pricing/commit options — action: Rafael

Please confirm the decision criteria and any missing requirements. If you want, we can schedule the perf test kickoff this week — otherwise we'll aim for the Feb 20 slot.

Thanks,

—

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the decision criteria: 

1) For streaming, when you say TTF target < 200 ms for first tokens, is that measured p95 or median? We need p95 for UI snappiness.
2) You noted p99 in the 350-450 ms range — can you confirm what you expect Redwood to guarantee for p99 under the 500 rps sustained load?

Hi Samir — great questions, thanks. Answers below: 

1) Streaming TTF measurement
- We measure TTF at p95 by default for production SLOs. For the AcmePay UI use-case I recommend you require p95 < 200 ms for first token. We can also provide median and p99 if you want additional visibility.

2) p99 under 500 rps sustained
- Based on the demo traces and our kernel/quantization profile, we expect p99 to be in the 350–450 ms range when the KV cache is warm. We'll include a 95% CI in the perf report. If p99 is a hard cutoff for you, let's set target p99 < 450 ms.

3) Cold-starts / warm pools
- We recommend a warm pool configured to cover your 8–10am peaks. With a warm pool sized for expected concurrency (we'll propose numbers after we see your session distribution) cold-starts should be rare. If a cold-start occurs, degraded latency will be expected (2–3x p95) unless you accept additional reserved capacity. We'll include cold-start test cases in the perf run so you can see impact.

Suggested decision criteria (please confirm):
- p95 interactive latency < 200 ms (streaming p95 for first token)
- p99 < 450 ms under 500 rps sustained
- 500 req/s sustained for 10+ minutes
- Support 100 concurrent sessions with warm pool

Next steps (updated)
- Redwood to provision test account + share perf test plan (link) — Marissa (by Feb 15)
- Run perf test with your payloads; include cold-start scenarios — Marissa / Dev (week of Feb 20)
- Redwood to produce perf report + recommendation for warm pool sizing — Marissa / Rafael (2 business days after test)
- If OK, spin up 2-week dedicated trial & pricing proposal — Rafael

I'll prepare the perf test configuration and share the link to the plan today. Are you available for a 30-minute kickoff on Feb 21 at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Marissa
